subject: SLA for async batch inference — completion windows & exception request
messages:
From: Elena Morales <contracts@datastream.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA for async batch inference — scope & exceptions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we map Redwood into our nightly ETL and inference pipeline, procurement and engineering need a clear SLA for async/batch jobs. Our specific asks:

- A formal completion window for batch jobs (e.g., X hours for small/medium/large job buckets).
- Clarity on retries and whether Redwood guarantees exactly-once, at-least-once, or allows dedup via idempotency tokens.
- Measurement methodology and what counts as a failure vs acceptable delay.
- An exception path for jobs that exceed the usual window during monthly peaks (we have spikes that can triple runtime).

Attached is a rough sample of our job size distribution and a starting SLA draft (SLA_Draft_v1.pdf). Can you confirm what you can commit to, and what you need from us (e.g., job IDs, checkpointing guidance, telemetry hooks)?

Best,
Elena
Contracts — DataStream Inc.

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <contracts@datastream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA for async batch inference — scope & exceptions

Elena,

Thanks — this is a good starting point. High level responses and proposed approach below; I'll loop in engineering for the implementation details.

Proposed SLA structure (initial suggestion):
- Job size buckets by input tokens / model compute (small: <=10k tokens, medium: 10k-100k, large: >100k).
- Completion windows (SLO targets): small — 30 min, medium — 4 hours, large — 12 hours. These are 95th-percentile monthly targets by default.
- Retry behavior: Redwood will perform transparent retries on transient infra errors using exponential backoff (default max attempts = 5) unless the customer opts-out. Customers must supply an idempotency key/job_id for deduplication when they require exactly-once semantics.
- Idempotency: exact-execute requires client-provided job_id and a dedupe TTL (recommendation: 48 hours). Without a job_id, behavior is best-effort at-most-once where duplicates may occur on retries.
- Exceptions: we can set an elevated completion window (up to 24 hrs) for named jobs with documented monthly peak patterns via an Exception SLA addendum + weekly review during the first 90 days.

Action items for DataStream (what we need):
1) Example job_id format and whether you can attach a checkpointing token per chunk.
2) Representative job size distribution (you already attached a sample — helpful).
3) A runbook for your retry/idempotency expectations.

I'll let Rohan add technical constraints and notes on logging/measurement. Marissa — can you own the commercial/exception addendum?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of GTM — Redwood Inference

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <contracts@datastream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA for async batch inference — scope & exceptions

Elena / Laura,

Technical clarifications from the infra side:

1) Measurement & completion definition:
   - "Completion" = all requested input records for a job have produced final tokens and final status recorded to our job-store.
   - We measure end-to-end latency from job submission time (t0) to final status write (tf). SLAs will be calculated on per-job per-month percentiles (95th).

2) Idempotency & semantics:
   - We support client-provided job_id (string) and chunk_id for chunked uploads. If provided, we guarantee dedup within a configurable TTL (default 48h).
   - Without job_id, retries may lead to duplicate executions (at-least-once) since retrying an interrupted model step may re-run tokens.

3) Retry policy & recommendations:
   - Redwood will retry transient infra errors with exponential backoff (initial 2s -> 4s -> 8s ... up to max attempts 5).
   - For long-running jobs, we recommend client-side checkpointing every N chunks so resumed runs pick up from last checkpoint rather than restart.

4) Edge cases / long tails:
   - If a job is starved for GPU capacity we will proactively route or burst to compatible capacity tiers where possible. For exceptionally large monthly peaks we propose a formal exception SLA with an extended completion window and pre-notified maintenance windows.

I've attached a short note on retry policy and idempotency parameters (retry_policy_notes.md). Happy to walk through a proposed instrumentation plan (hooks + events) with your engineers.

-Rohan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <contracts@datastream.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA for async batch inference — scope & exceptions

Thanks, team. A couple follow-ups:

- Our nightly ETL+inference job (JobName: monthly-enrich) usually finishes in ~6-8 hours most days but can spike to 20+ hours on month-ends. We need a path to avoid penalties during those expected spikes but still want guarantees the job will not be silently dropped or reprocessed causing duplicates.
- Can Redwood support an exception SLA for monthly-enrich that extends the completion window to 24 hours and provides stronger logging/traceability?
- If we need to provide job_id + checkpoint tokens, what's the recommended format and how long must we retain those job IDs for dedup?

Attached is a sample month of runtime stats (monthly_job_stats_sample.csv). Also please confirm whether SLA calculations will include jobs that get retried vs killed and how credits would be computed if targets are missed.

-Elena

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <contracts@datastream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA for async batch inference — scope & exceptions

Elena — we can support an Exception SLA for your monthly-enrich workload with the following guardrails:

1) Extended completion window: up to 24 hours for named job(s) under the Exception SLA (measured as before, t0 -> tf).
2) Required instrumentation: client-provided job_id (string UUID recommended) and optional chunk_id/checkpoint token for resume. Dedup TTL = 72 hours for Exception SLAs (we can shorten if you prefer).
3) Retry behavior: Redwood retains default retry policy (exp backoff, max attempts 5) but for Exception SLAs we'll increase max attempts to 8 and extend backoff ceiling.
4) Monitoring & runbook: you and Redwood must agree to a runbook (alert thresholds, escalation contacts). For Exception SLAs we will provision a weekly sync in the first 90 days and provide a shared trace dashboard.
5) Credits & measurement: SLA will be computed on a per-job-month basis at the 95th percentile. If the 95th percentile exceeds the agreed window for that month, credit = (percentage over target) * monthly service fee * 0.25 (example formula; legal to finalize).

Next steps:
- Marissa: please draft the commercial addendum for an Exception SLA and flag anything that changes pricing.
- Dev (procurement): please confirm if this exception language and the credits formula are acceptable to legal/procurement.
- Rohan: please confirm the implementation timeline to add the 72h dedupe TTL and extended retry parameters for exception profiles.

If all agree we'll move to a short addendum and DocuSign.

Thanks,
Laura

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <contracts@datastream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA for async batch inference — scope & exceptions

Elena / team,

We can accept the Exception SLA approach in principle but need the contract clause to be explicit on the following items before we sign:

1) Measurement methodology: define whether jobs that fail and are retried count as separate jobs or the same job for percentile computation. We prefer counting unique job_id timeframe (i.e., retries are part of same job measurement).
2) Credit calculation formula must be deterministic in the contract (sample formula OK but should be final in the addendum).
3) Runbook attachment: the addendum must reference an agreed runbook stored in the shared Drive and require both parties to maintain it.
4) Data retention: required retention period for job_id/dedupe metadata (we'll settle at 90 days for auditability).

Marissa — please prepare the DocuSign addendum with: exception window (24h), dedupe TTL (72h), measurement method (unique job_id), credits formula, runbook link.

Elena — once you confirm the runbook link and accept the 90-day retention we can route to signature.

-Dev
Head of Procurement Operations — Redwood Inference
